title: Treat Git as process, not file storage
trigger: The assistant is asked to commit, push, merge, branch, open a PR, or otherwise handle repository state.
steps: Identify the current branch and working tree state.
Identify the intended integration branch and release branch before changing repository topology.
Keep feature work isolated until it is ready to merge into the integration branch.
Use commits, pushes, merges, and pull requests to move work through the agreed process.
gates: Do not describe Git as merely saving files.
Do not push random feature branches and call the work integrated.
Do not merge to master directly unless the user explicitly overrides the project process.
evidence: The PR base and head match the project workflow.
text: For FrustLang, Git is a workflow and coordination system, not a file store. Before doing Git operations, Frusty must understand the branch process: feature work belongs on feature branches, integration happens on the project integration branch, and release movement happens through a pull request to master. A commit pushed to an arbitrary feature branch is not complete integration. Always report which branch was changed, which branch was pushed, and whether a PR was opened.

title: Use development as the Codex integration branch
trigger: The assistant is doing Codex-originated development work in FrustLang.
authority: User instruction: Codex uses development as its integration/build branch, creates feature branches from it, merges feature branches back to development, then opens a PR to master when ready.
steps: Start from the latest development branch.
Create a focused feature branch from development for the change.
Commit the feature work on that feature branch.
Merge the feature branch back into development after the work is ready.
Push development to origin.
Open a pull request from development to master when the user wants the work promoted.
gates: Do not use a randomly named feature branch as the final integration branch.
Do not ask the user to care about temporary feature branch names when they asked for integrated work.
Do not directly PR a feature branch to master unless the user explicitly asks for that exception.
evidence: git status shows development clean after merge.
The PR head is development and the PR base is master.
text: In FrustLang, Codex's durable integration branch is development. Feature branches are temporary working branches created from development. When feature work is ready, merge it back into development and push development. When the user says to PR the work into master, open the PR from development to master. Do not leave the user with only a strangely named feature branch pushed to origin and call that complete.

title: Use before and after Git checks
trigger: The assistant is about to change repository state or report repository completion.
steps: Before repository operations, run a concise status check to confirm branch and cleanliness.
After commit, record the commit hash and message.
After push, confirm the branch pushed successfully.
Before final reporting, check that the intended branch is clean and tracking origin.
gates: Do not run destructive Git commands such as reset or checkout over changes unless explicitly authorized.
Do not revert unrelated user work.
Do not claim a branch is pushed without evidence from Git.
evidence: Status output shows the expected branch.
Push output names the remote branch.
Final status is clean or accurately reports remaining work.
text: For FrustLang repository work, Frusty should perform concise before/after Git checks. Before changing repository state, know the branch and whether the tree is clean. After committing, report the commit hash. After pushing, know which remote branch was updated. Before final completion, confirm the intended branch is clean and tracking origin. Never use destructive Git operations to make the tree look clean.

title: Treat FrustLang as a production repository
trigger: The assistant is working in D:\FrustLang or any FrustLang repository checkout.
authority: User instruction: FrustLang is a production repository.
steps: Assume branch process matters.
Prefer scoped changes and focused commits.
Keep generated experiments out of production paths unless they are intentional project artifacts.
Use the development integration branch for Codex work.
Promote to master only through reviewed pull request flow.
gates: Do not leave experimental throwaway directories committed unless they are intentionally part of the test/eval system.
Do not push unreviewed integration directly to master.
Do not treat local convenience as more important than repository hygiene.
evidence: Branch movement follows the FrustLang process.
Completion report names the branch, commit, push, and PR state.
text: FrustLang is a production repository. Frusty must treat repository hygiene, branch flow, and promotion process as part of the work. Source changes, generated cards, docs, tests, and experiments must have a reason to live in the repository. Codex work integrates through development and moves to master by pull request.

title: Use frusty-test as the Git learning sandbox
trigger: The assistant is working in a repository named frusty-test or the user asks Frusty to practice Git behavior.
authority: User intent: frusty-test is a safe training repository where Frusty can practice Git, make mistakes, recover, and learn process without risking production work.
steps: Treat the repository as a sandbox, not production.
Practice explicit branch, commit, merge, conflict, revert, and PR flows.
Record what happened and what was learned after each exercise.
Prefer recoverable mistakes and visible evidence over pretending everything went perfectly.
gates: Do not transfer sandbox looseness to FrustLang or other production repositories.
Do not use real secrets, customer data, or production release credentials in the sandbox.
Do not hide mistakes; mistakes are training data when recorded truthfully.
evidence: Final report explains the branch flow, commands/results, mistakes, recovery, and lesson learned.
text: frusty-test is the safe Git learning sandbox for Frusty. In that repository, Frusty may practice Git process, make recoverable mistakes, learn from them, and record lessons. This sandbox permission does not apply to FrustLang or other production repositories. The point is to teach Git as process: branch intent, commit purpose, merge flow, PR behavior, recovery, and truthful evidence.
